How does someone get a SIGNED certificate for a user that doesn't exist on the host?  That sounds like a bug in the intermediate authority if it's issuing credentials for invalid users?

Hi Ed, sorry just got time to get back to this

so in our case, this can happen because we reuse our certificate. basically everyone at the company has correct format certificate, but not everyone has access to the BMC
- to be more specific: we issue x509 cert where we put SAN UPN for everyone with the same correct format. but we only store few accounts to the phosphor user manager

here we leverage the accounts/users from phosphor user manager service. if the user doesn't exist in the user manager service, the request will fail

however, currently it would be marked as 500 as it fails during GetUserInfo. previously I intended to try to validate whether the username from the cert exist in the user manager service, but it seems like it's quite hard to do (callback refactoring) + will be double fetching

here I propose to differentiate the http code response from the error code that we get when we try to contact user manager

- if the error code is io error -> return unauthorized
- if the error code is no route to host (user manager service) -> return 5xx code

let me know what do you think, thanks!

Thank you very much for your time and consideration. I look forward to hearing your inputs!

Best regards,
Malik Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani

> so in our case, this can happen because we reuse our certificate

There's a hostname in the certificate UPN, how do you reuse a CN between two different machines if there's a hostname?  This part isn't the most important to this patch, it was just something I was curious about.

FYI, your current patch doesn't pass CI, and the last revision I reviewed didn't work at all, so generally it doesn't show up on the list to review until it does.  If you need help on getting it to pass CI, I'm always available on the mailing list and discord.

As you described it, the behavior sounds fine fine, just make sure we're not taking an extra overhead to create those error codes.  If the goal is to avoid side channel determining a users existence, changing the timing give as much indication that a user exists as the error code.
Unaddressed

Hi Ed and Gunnar, sorry I think I missed this comment, 

> There's a hostname in the certificate UPN, how do you reuse a CN between two different machines if there's a hostname?

We only put top part of the hostname tree inside the UPN. For example, let's say we have this hostname `switch010.dc01.region03.example.com`. We only put `malikrafsan@example.com` inside the UPN. This will ensure that we can make the UPN to access all devices that we have

Hi Ed! yup, today I just re-tested both path! Also, I am sorry I should put 401 instead of 404 there (was working on something else and not too focus, sorry!)

here are my full test plan that I just executed:

## path of 401 http code
### modified device
- deploy new image to a BMC test device
- remove account from bmcweb (`curl -X DELETE .../AccountService/Accounts/<removed-acc>`)
- use certificate of removed account (`curl --cert=... --key=... .../AccountService/Accounts -v`)
- expect to get 401

### controlled device
- remove account from bmcweb (`curl -X DELETE .../AccountService/Accounts/<removed-acc>`)
- use certificate of removed account (`curl --cert=... --key=... .../AccountService/Accounts -v`)
- expect to get 500

---

## path of 500 http code
### stopped phosphor-user-manager service
- re-add removed account to the modified BMC device using root user (`curl --user="root:<root-pwd>" --data=<json-to-readd-removed-acc> -X POST .../AccountService/Accounts`)
- ssh to the BMC
- stop the phosphor-user-manager srv (`systemctl stop xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager`)
- send curl request (`curl --cert=... --key=... .../AccountService/Accounts -v`)
- expect to get 500

### healthy phosphor-user-manager service
- restart the phosphor-user-manager srv inside modified BMC (`systemctl start xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager`)
- ensure that the service is healthy (`systemctl status xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager`)
- send curl request (`curl --cert=... --key=... .../AccountService/Accounts -v`)
- expect to get 200 (and response)

---

Please let me know if the test plan is not covering necessary cases, thank you!!

Oh also testing of the path of 500 http code on controlled device (control variable / BMC that I don't modify):

## path of 500 http code
### controlled device
- ssh to the BMC
- stop the phosphor-user-manager srv (`systemctl stop xyz.openbmc_project.User.Manager`)
- send curl request (`curl --cert=... --key=... .../AccountService/Accounts -v`)
- expect to get 500 (same as the modified BMC, as expected)
